findings.reason: the accepted grammar must be settled in the plan text (indexed like imas.util output, or unindexed with an explicit rule for what "one per filled signal the path names" yields when a struct array is named), which fixes the interface the whole node is built against.
findings.text: DD path resolution is owned by imas-python's imas.util (`get_full_path`, `get_parent`, `visit_children`, `tree_iter`), but §1 defines its own path grammar whose examples (`coil/current`, `flux_loop/flux`, `ip`) carry no array index, while the owner renders the same node as `coil[0]/current` (verified: `imas.util.get_full_path(pf.coil[0].current)` returns `coil[0]/current`); the plan also never states whether an indexed path is accepted, and this is the only path-resolution site in the change, so a path obtained from the owner (or one written with an index) does not round-trip and the function silently returns the wrong series set

response_events.reason: §1 now fixes the grammar: the path is the unindexed data-dictionary path IDSMetadata.path renders (coil/current), naming a quantity; the function returns one series per element of every struct array on the path; an instance path holding '[' (as imas.util.get_full_path renders coil[0]/current) raises ValueError naming the unindexed form, with a test in the done-when

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one two-argument public function hides the whole of the behaviour: the DD-path walk through struct arrays, three time-base modes, unit read, y-label selection and empty-element skipping, all behind `(ids, path)`; the interfaces it returns (`TimeSeries`) and feeds (`time_trace_figure_mpl`) already exist and are unchanged.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan invents a bespoke DD-path grammar rather than adopting the resolution semantics imas-python already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 states in its own text that it adds one public name and retires nothing, and that `TimeSeries` and the equilibrium extractor stay as they are, so the one added definition is accounted for and no existing surface is duplicated.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan cites the machinery it extends (`extract_time_traces` and the `TimeSeries` type in `imas_ink/extract.py` and `imas_ink/components.py`, fed unchanged to `time_trace_figure_mpl`), and an independent search of imas-ink and imas-python found no pre-existing signal reader or path-string resolver to reuse.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the function reads IDS leaves that no current reader touches (`pf_active/coil/current`, `magnetics/flux_loop/flux`, `magnetics/ip` values); `extract_time_traces` reads only equilibrium global scalars and `extract_geometry` reads probe/flux-loop positions but no signal data, so there is no existing reader to extend instead.
